text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak and Chirac talks affirm their agreement on steps needed to revive Middle East peace process. France shares Egypt's worry over lack of commitment from United States in some issues.
- Jospin affirms to Mubarak his government's support for peace efforts.
- EU envoy Moratinos says Egypt and Europe are working from same understanding of peace.

- Amid crisis between U.S. adminstration and Congress, U.S. spokesman says U.S. rejects any measures to change status of Jerusalem and affirmed his country's appreciation for Egypt's efforts, saying U.S. would not allow the peace process to be buried.
- Senate sub-committee approves stoppage of aid for Egypt.
- African information ministers at close of their meeting in Cairo say they appreciate Egypt's role in spearheading communication issues in Africa.
- Army chief says peace does not mean taking things too easy; says Egyptian armed forces believe in modernisation.
- After prison term for British thief who stole Egyptian antiquities, British police say it is Egypt's right to ask for return of its other stolen treasures.
- Egypt greets its golden butterfly swimmer Rania Elwani with flowers after she wins gold medal at Mediterranean games.
- Unified labour law to go before parliament at its next session.
- Boy who got separated from his mother during Haj fire reunited with her in Cairo.
